claims.text: Chemical short-range order typically suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys relative to a random solid solution.
The proposed conductivity suppression is caused primarily by enhanced phonon scattering at SRO clusters.
At very high temperatures, SRO may dissolve or become dynamic.
The effect of SRO on lattice thermal conductivity diminishes at high temperature, where baseline disorder scattering dominates.
MoNbTaW is a body-centered-cubic refractory high-entropy alloy.
MoNbTaW can exhibit a significant energetic driving force for chemical SRO.
Rapid quenching from the melt or fast cooling after high-temperature annealing produces a disordered RHEA state with negligible SRO.
Intermediate-temperature annealing below the order-disorder transition enhances SRO without producing long-range precipitates.
SRO is stable over 300–1000 K in the proposed refractory-alloy regime.
Atomic-size mismatch and negative enthalpy of mixing favor SRO in refractory multicomponent alloys.
Non-random chemical SRO can be quantified using Warren-Cowley SRO parameters that deviate from the random-state value.
SRO clusters create local variations in atomic mass, bond stiffness, and force constants that act as phonon-scattering centers.
Mass-difference scattering and bond-stiffness variations associated with SRO reduce the phonon mean free path.
SRO adds a secondary phonon-scattering mechanism beyond the configurational-disorder scattering already present in the random alloy.
At higher temperatures, anharmonic phonon-phonon scattering dominates and reduces the relative influence of SRO.
The decrease in lattice thermal conductivity increases with the measured degree of SRO.
SRO-induced suppression of lattice thermal conductivity is most pronounced from 300 to 800 K.
Thermal transport in the random reference state is dominated by mass variance and lattice distortion caused by random atomic arrangements.
Above the order-disorder transition, dissolution of SRO returns thermal conductivity to the random-state baseline.
Growth of SRO clusters into long-range ordered precipitates shifts transport toward band-structure or interface-scattering effects and may change the conductivity trend.

contradictions.description: The conditions field describes SRO as stable throughout 300–1000 K, while the hypothesis and boundary allow SRO to dissolve at high temperature, and the uncertainty field says the temperature at which SRO becomes negligible is unknown. No transition temperature is specified to reconcile these statements.
